claims.statement: IAEA clinical-audit guidance includes a dental-practice quality-assurance program and repeat analysis among the items to review.
EU guidance says software qualification and classification under MDR or IVDR depends on intended purpose regardless of whether the software runs on a phone, in the cloud, or elsewhere.

contrary_evidence: Imaging hardware and PACS vendors may already include exposure and quality-control features.
A clinic's repeat rate may be too low for the subscription to show rapid financial payback.

economics.acquisition_route: Start with retrospective, de-identified images and repeat logs from one reseller's consenting clinics; obtain a formal regulatory classification opinion before live use.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 1800 units at 400 PLN monthly net revenue yield 8.64m PLN ARR; at 30% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 60% founder ownership, equity is about 6.2m PLN in year 7-10. Retained earnings are not counted again.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 12-18 hours weekly, with a dental radiologist, medical physicist, and regulatory specialist engaged only for a funded validation stage.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 72-82% after channel share, inference, secure storage, support, and validation monitoring.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 20000-50000 PLN per reseller integration recovered within 8-14 months at 20-35 live units.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 250-600 PLN per imaging unit monthly, with 20-30% retained by the equipment or PACS reseller.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Licenses renew with annual equipment service; every acquisition provides a usage and QA event.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Device-specific images linked to accept-repeat labels, technician feedback, and service outcomes improve QA models
fingerprint.customer: Dental practices operating digital radiography equipment supplied or serviced by a reseller
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Dental equipment and PACS resellers bundle the module at installation and service renewal
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Non-diagnostic acquisition-quality flags, repeat analytics, and training reports licensed per device
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Clinic or reseller pays a recurring per-device license bundled into the equipment service contract
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An image is acquired with a technical quality defect or a clinic's repeat rate drifts upward

founder_fit: Image-quality modelling is adjacent to the founder's neuroscience, biosignal, and data background.
Equipment resellers provide concentrated distribution and can perform clinic support.
A retrospective, non-live pilot can test feasibility before spending on regulatory work.
risks: Regulatory classification and conformity assessment could exceed bootstrap capital.
False reassurance could allow a poor-quality image to enter clinical use.
PACS and equipment integration may be vendor-specific and security-sensitive.

structure.control_point: Technical image-quality and repeat-outcome history tied to each installed device
structure.critical_dependency: Sufficient labeled image data and a regulatory path compatible with bootstrap staging

thesis: Provide dental X-ray equipment and PACS resellers a per-device quality-assurance module that flags likely positioning, blur, clipping, and exposure-quality problems immediately, tracks repeat rates, and creates technician training reports. It does not detect disease or recommend care. The reseller bundles it with service contracts, gains a differentiated renewal product, and supplies repeated clinic access; confirmed repeats and service outcomes create a device-specific QA dataset.
title: Dental Imaging Acquisition QA Through Equipment Resellers
uncertainties: Which acquisition defects can be identified reliably without interpreting pathology?
Can a reseller supply enough labeled accept-repeat outcomes for validation?
Will regulators view operational QA as medical-device software or an accessory?
